text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH 429/503 spike detected for inference-prod (since 2129876000). Top affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings. Paging on-call.

jess: I'm on it. seeing a large cluster of 429s in the last 3m. dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/abc123/429-503-live?orgId=1

mike: grabbing logs now. is this global or region-specific? I see EU is noisier.

anya: passenger telemetry shows sustained queue lengths on gpu-pool-7 and a sudden drop in worker availability around 2129875800.

jess: customer impact: CS says 3 customers reported elevated errors for batch embed jobs. QPS across system up ~2.8x from baseline.

ryan: rolling mitigation suggestion: 1) apply temporary tenant QPS cap to noisy tenants 2) enable short circuit for non-critical streaming features 3) increase request timeout fallback to reduce 503 churn.

mike: agree. start with surgical tenant caps. can you list top tenants by 429% contribution?

jess: pulling top offenders:
- tenant-id: ten-92 (35% of 429s)
- tenant-id: ten-01 (22%)
- tenant-id: ten-77 (9%)

anya: ten-92 has large batched embedding jobs—could be a misconfigured retry loop.

jess: executing cap for ten-92 to 30 qps (was unlimited). command:
```
curl -s -X POST "https://ops-api.internal/tenants/ten-92/ratecap" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \ 
  -d '{"qps":30, "duration_secs":900, "reason":"emergency live-shape 429 spike"}'
```

mike: patch applied and acknowledged by control-plane. watching metrics.

incident-bot: action logged by jess at 2129876900.

jess: also disabling non-critical streaming hooks for rollout-id stream-xyz (this reduces connection churn). command:
```
redwoodctl feature disable --target stream-xyz --env prod --reason "mitigate connection churn"
```

ryan: queued a canary route to fallback model small-v2 for embeddings-heavy routes to reduce kernel pressure.

anya: telemetry: 429% contribution from ten-92 dropped from 35% -> 8% in the first 2m after cap. cluster queue length down 48%.

mike: nice. 503s still present but trending down. we should also increase the per-worker queue limit to avoid abrupt 503s. patching worker config:
```
kubectl -n inference-prod patch configmap worker-config -p '{"data":{"max_inflight":"150"}}'
```

jess: patch rolled. rebooting 3 pods gracefully to pick up config.

mike: pods restarted. 503 rate went from 2.1% -> 0.4% over 6m. latency stable.

jess: contacting CS with a short update: "We've applied temporary rate caps and routing fallbacks; 429/503 rates significantly reduced. We'll keep caps in place while we investigate root cause."

ryan: brief note — keep an eye on billing effects (burst to fallback model could change unit cost). tagging finance for visibility.

anya: started a short-term eval run to reproduce misbehaving client retry. logs show a client performing concurrent batch retries without jitter.

mike: next steps: 1) keep caps for 15m 2) collect traces from ten-92 3) open a follow-up with infra/solutions to block runaway retry patterns.

jess: i'm going to hand off to mike for the rest of the on-call window. mike — you taking the pager?

mike: taking it. will monitor dashboards and add playbook notes. moving the thread to an oncall-handoff tag.

incident-bot: oncall-handoff documented by mike at 2129878600.

mike: summary for postmortem: sudden client-side retry surge + a large batched embedding workload caused queue exhaustion on gpu-pool-7 -> elevated 429/503. mitigations (rate caps, feature disables, worker queue bump) reduced 429s from peak 8.6% to 0.6% and 503s from 2.1% to 0.3% within 10m.

jess: leaving notes in incident tracker: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-754

ryan: i'll notify affected account managers and ask CS to reach out to the three reporting customers.

anya: saving collected traces and logs to s3: s3://redwood-incident-archives/2129876543/trace-bundle.gz

mike: if anything spikes again, we escalate to infra and consider temporarily enabling global rate limiter for unsafe endpoints.

jess: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

mike: closing temporary actions after 15m if metrics stay stable; will update this thread and the tracker.

incident-bot: thread closed for monitoring at 2129880200.
